notes: Matches the skill run almost point-for-point; least differentiated case; fewest tool calls (2)

Pass rate is identical (100%) in both configurations across all 3 evals — the assertions check RECALL of the 3 planted violations, and unaided Claude in this repo already finds all of them (it can read the root and server/ CLAUDE.md, which name Onion, SecretsProvider, vendor/shared's two copies and arch:check). The assertions are non-discriminating for this skill on these fixtures.

Where the skill changes the output is PRECISION and VOCABULARY, which the current assertions don't score: with-skill reviews cite specific rule numbers, the import-legality table, and numbered anti-patterns; they are shorter and prioritised (3 CRITICAL + lesser) vs the baseline's flatter 7-8 item lists.

Strongest skill-only insight observed: eval-1 with_skill flags that the Slack port belongs in server/src/ports/ rather than vendor/shared *because vendor/shared is vendored into the browser bundle's type surface* — baseline flags the placement but not this reason.

eval-2 (reviewer-core purity) is the least differentiated: baseline and skill outputs are nearly identical. I/O-in-the-domain is a widely-known clean-architecture rule, so the skill adds little there.
Cost of the skill: ~+30% tokens (~+10.9k) and ~+6s per review, for no recall gain on these fixtures.

To make this benchmark discriminating, the fixtures need violations that are repo-specific and subtle (e.g. a port that looks fine but leaks one vendor noun; a service taking Container that produces a real dependency cycle only because the container also builds it; a baseline-regeneration to silence arch:check) and assertions that score whether the review names the correct rule and the correct fix location, not just 'mentions the problem'.

Also worth adding: a negative/adversarial fixture that is actually correct, to check the skill doesn't invent violations (all 6 runs here scored the 'no invented violations' assertion as pass, but nothing tested a clean input).
